description: Conformance vectors for weir-attest's chain construction: H0 = SHA256(domain_sep ++ prev_head ++ format_version ++ shard_id LE u16 ++ created_at LE i64 ++ len(segment_name) LE u64 ++ segment_name), RecordId = SHA256(len(segment) LE u64 ++ segment ++ index LE u64 ++ len(payload) LE u64 ++ payload) with a 1-based index, and Hi = SHA256(H(i-1) ++ RecordId_i). Generated independently of crates/weir-attest — this file computes every hash from the spec using stdlib hashlib, sharing no code and no constants by import with the Rust implementation it checks.

vectors.name: single_record_chain
vectors.notes: The smallest possible chain: one record. Pins H0 and a single chain_step together — get either the domain separator, the header field order, or the fold wrong and this already fails, before any multi-record vector below gets a chance to.
vectors.head: d46abe750ad385157aeb5f1dfa15a4b3fe453afd1913f5d7f4af83907470328a

vectors.name: three_record_chain
vectors.notes: Three records folded in sequence. Pins that h_1, h_2 and the final head (h_3) are each SHA256(previous head ++ that record's RecordId) computed in order — not three independent digests, and not folded out of order.
vectors.head: 6e8cbc60873ffad4b66fc7b9eb3eaae79f71e7232d653ade65b16e4d5e2afc42

vectors.name: three_record_chain_different_segment_name
vectors.notes: Identical prev_head, header and three records as 'three_record_chain' — only segment_name changes (…seg_00000001 -> …seg_00000002). Both H0 (which folds the name directly) and every RecordId (which folds the segment a record was read from) depend on it, so the head MUST differ. Catches an implementation that forgets to fold the segment name into H0, or that computes RecordId without it.
vectors.head: 90437711ff44d4f058ee40c1c57dfc83458f2a93138b6b3332fcc7eb639cd18e

vectors.name: three_record_chain_reordered
vectors.notes: Identical prev_head, header, segment_name and three records as 'three_record_chain' — only the ORDER changes (a rotation: gamma, alpha, beta). RecordId's index is a record's 1-based POSITION within the segment, so reordering reassigns every index as well as the fold order; the resulting head must differ both from 'three_record_chain' and from what an implementation would get if it reordered the fold but forgot to recompute each record's index for its new position.
vectors.head: df28e551df0298d7b07bcbb3c7b5bb84bdbb973251a2c747fec439c424a404d0

vectors.name: nonzero_prev_head
vectors.notes: prev_head is a non-zero, non-repeating 32-byte pattern (bytes 0x00..0x1f) rather than ChainHead::ORIGIN, so an implementation that silently hardcodes the origin as H0's predecessor fails here even though every vector above it (all origin-rooted) would still pass. shard_id is 0x1234, whose little-endian encoding (34 12) is not a palindrome, and created_at is -1 (all-ones once sign-extended to 8 bytes) — both chosen so a byte-order mistake or an unsigned-i64 mistake changes the digest rather than coincidentally matching.
vectors.head: 73eb509d7a1ee07bef986e9606bf4927066c3fbacefc85c4d79023c64a80398b
